name: The Walker household — a documented justice of the peace, unplaced in the town
head: walker_james

arrival.note: A BOUND FROM THE PAPER, NOT AN ARRIVAL. The corpus first prints this person at the Democrat of 26 November 1833, column 31, so they are in the town's paper by 1833-11-26 and at no stated time before it; nothing reached says when they came. Last printed 1833-11-26.

lives_at.note: Not attested. NOTHING IS BEING WITHHELD HERE: no source reached says where this person lived, and 52 households in this dataset were already in that position before this one was written.

works_at.note: Not attested as a structure this project models. The trade is documented; the premises are not one of the committed records.

present_on_scene_date.note: THE CORPUS STOPS BEFORE THE SCENE DATE. Last printed 1833-11-26, at the Democrat of 26 November 1833, column 31, and nothing reached either follows this person to 1 July 1835 or says they left. A documented resident whose whereabouts on one day are unknown is `uncertain` here rather than dropped: that is the same distinction index.json draws for Jeremiah Porter, and it is a finding rather than a gap.

persons.name: James Walker

occupation.note: THE TRADE IS THE PAPER'S. The corpus reads it as justice of the peace, at the Democrat of 26 November 1833, column 31. The residents vocabulary's nearest period-correct word for it is `justice_of_the_peace`, and where the corpus prints more than one trade they are all named here rather than reduced to the one the vocabulary could take.

persons.note: A DOCUMENTED PERSON, AND NOTHING ELSE IS CLAIMED. The papers name 'James Walker, J. P.' and give the trade; they do not say where this household lived, who else was in it, or when it came. So the record around this person carries nothing but the person: no dwelling, no division, no family, each written as unattested in its own block rather than filled in from the shape of the rest of the town. Cited at the Democrat of 26 November 1833, column 31. THE TOWN NEVER INVENTED A ROOF FOR THIS TRADE. The occupation census raised reconstructed households for the trades a town of 3,265 people needed and could not document; `justice_of_the_peace` was not one of them, which is why this person could only ever be ADDED and never seated on an existing record — data/research/newspapers/register_1835.json calls it `new_resident` for exactly that reason. No figure is drawn (docs/LIBERTIES.md L1). READ THROUGH A TRANSCRIPTION, not a scan: the owner's ruling of 2026-08-28 grades a transcription-mediated reading as documented, and the source record for the run states that standard and its limits. A scan read that confirms or corrects the name upgrades this entry. THE FEDERAL LAND TRACT SALES — A PURCHASE, AND NEVER A RESIDENCE. The Illinois State Archives' Public Domain Land Tract Sales register enters this person 2 times, as “WALKER JAMES”, 1830-10-04: 2 lots in the platted town — lot 4 of block 10 in the town the register codes CHIOT (L4BL10CHIOT, as printed); lot 4 of block 19 in the town the register codes CHIOT (L4BL19CHIOT, as printed), 0.00 acres stated in all, for $56.00 (ls1528, ls1529). THE REGISTER'S OWN RESIDENCE COLUMN READS UNKNOWN on these rows: a county, a state or nothing, and never a town, which is why a purchase here places nobody. THE TOWN LOTS ARE THE PLAT ITSELF, AND THEY ARE NOT ACRES: Cook County's register describes them by lot and block in a platted town and gives them no section, no township and no acreage at all, so they add nothing to the acre figure above and $56.00 to the money. This project does not expand the register's town codes, so which addition a lot stands in is carried as the code and not as a name. It is still a purchase and it still places nobody. A purchase and nothing more. It dates and places a transaction; it proposes no residence, and under the ratified ladder it corroborates rather than mints. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: WALKER JAMES matches James Walker: the forename names James Walker of the 4 people of this surname, and the forename agrees in full. (data/research/land_sales/resident_crosswalk.json). This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and a land entry is a second source about a TRANSACTION rather than about who was living at Chicago on 1 July 1835 — a man may buy a quarter-section he never sees. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict.

roles.note: THE BOUND IS THE SOURCE'S, NOT THE MAN'S. This role is carried by the card's 1835 occupation block and is dated by what the cited source or sources are ABOUT, which is why `precision` can be no better than the span they cover. The span reaches 1835, so this role stands in the scene-date view. The printing the trade was read off is not on the card and is fetched by T-1254.

merge_ruling.for_merge: F against W is one letter to a distance, and the initial J agrees with both James Walker the justice of the peace. 'Falker' is set nowhere at all in the deposited corpus, which is the profile of a mis-read surname rather than a family.
merge_ruling.against_merge: THE INITIAL J HAS TWO RIVALS AND THE SAME COLUMN PRINTS THEM BOTH. The Democrat of 26 November 1833, column 31, sets 'Walker, James' and 'Walker, Jeremiah' — two Walkers of this town whose forenames both begin with J, in one printing. An initial with two rivals attaches to neither: R2. The town holds four Walker cards in all (walker_george_e, walker_george_h, walker_james, walker_jeremiah) and the surname is set 396 times in the corpus, while 'J. B. Falker' is one post-office reading of 1 July 1835 (#c006) with a middle initial B that neither Walker carries. Refused by a ratified rule; no ballot needed.

research_note: MINTED FROM THE NEWSPAPER REGISTER (T-0376), AND THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER RATHER THAN AN ARGUMENT. Every other record in this dataset argues for a household — a family the sources count, or a trade the town demonstrably needed. This one argues for a PERSON: the Democrat and the American name James Walker as a justice of the peace at Chicago 1 time(s), and this reconstruction did not hold them. `data/residents/` has no way to carry a person except inside a household, so one was written around them and told to claim nothing: one member, no dwelling, no division, no origin, no arrival beyond the bound the paper sets. Reading a family, a house or a quarter of town into this record would be reading something the papers do not say. tools/mint_documented_residents.py derives the whole minted set and prints every candidate it refused, with the reason.
